messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: SLO breach detected for /v1/generate (p99 latency > 2.5s) — triggered at 2026-03-14T10:13:09Z. Paging #eng-oncall :rotating_light:

ashley (oncall): on it — seeing p95 ~600ms but p99 spiking to ~3.8s. Streaming sessions show stalls/partial frames. Reproducing in staging? not yet, starting surface triage.

jonas: I can take traces. tagging @mia for routing/traffic. Any recent rollouts?

mia: yes, we pushed model v10-canary to 15% traffic ~10m before the alert. Canary config uses continuous-batching=true and new kernel selection heuristic.

ashley (oncall): ok, looks like correlation. Quick check: are fallback policies enabled? should fallback to v9-quant if latency high.

ops-runner: fallback policy is enabled, but logs show no fallback triggers for the last 12 minutes. See snippet from router logs:

```
2026-03-14T10:09:10Z router INFO route=canary-traffic decision=route_to v=10 node=rt-5
2026-03-14T10:12:41Z router WARN request_id=abc123 latency=3800ms model=v10 kernel=auto reason=no_fallback_match
```

mia: hmm router decision tree didn't match fallback because v10 reported compatible response shape. Fallback is gated on tail-latency rules, but it only triggers once errors exceed threshold — high latency doesn't equal error.

jonas: streaming stalls are concerning — KV cache thrash? runtime logs show repeated cache fills and evictions during v10 sessions.

ops-runner: runtime excerpt:
```
[2026-03-14T10:11:02Z] runtime WARN kv_cache miss_rate=0.84 eviction_rate=0.37 model=v10 shard=3
[2026-03-14T10:11:03Z] runtime WARN long_kernel_switch seq=256 time=120ms model=v10
```

ashley (oncall): customer impact check: no 5xx spike, but several customers report UI hangs in streaming editors (partial frames). I see ~12 high-traffic orgs had elevated tail latency. Not yet a full outage, but SLO breach.

mia: immediate mitigation options:
- shift canary down to 0% traffic
- enable emergency fallback by treating p99>2s as failure for routing policy (force fallback to v9)
- rollback the v10 canary (preferred if we expect regressions)

jonas: I can take manual rollback if ops confirm. What's the quickest reversible action?

ops-runner: quickest is traffic shift. Command to adjust traffic split via orchestration API:
```
POST /orchestrator/traffic
payload: {"model":"v10","target_percent":0}
```
I'll run that now.

ops-runner: running: `curl -X POST https://orchestrator.internal/api/traffic -d '{"model":"v10","target_percent":0}'` -> 202 Accepted.

deploy-bot: ACTION: Traffic shift started for model v10 -> 0%. Old route (v9) receiving ramped traffic.

ashley (oncall): monitoring p99 in real time. Give it a minute. Also leaving note: if p99 doesn't drop within 2 minutes, we will roll back release and open a regression for kernel heuristics.

~90s later~

mia: p99 dropped to 1.1s, p95 steady ~580ms. Streaming stalls count down by ~80%. Dashboard: https://dashboards.redwood/internal/slo/requests?span=5m&model=v10 (priv link)

jonas: rolling rollback anyway to be safe or keep v10 disabled and iterate? Thoughts?

ashley (oncall): since traffic shift restored SLOs and no data corruption, we'll leave v10 at 0% and mark rollout paused. Need root cause: kernel selection + KV cache behaviour on v10 weights. Assign to eng-runtime and eng-ml. I'm going to hand off live investigation to Jonas for deeper follow-up — oncall remains Ashley but Jonas leading postmortem.

jonas: taking follow-up — notes for oncall: capture runtime profiles for v10 traces, KV eviction heatmaps, BPF stack traces on affected nodes (rt-3/rt-5), and sample requests IDs: abc123, def456, ghi789. Also collect continuous-batching metrics (batch sizes, max wait).

mia: logging created: ENG-INC-2026-312

mia: small customer impact summary for comms: 
- scope: increased p99 latency and streaming stalls affecting partial frame delivery for a subset of streaming sessions (no 5xxs)
- timeframe: 2026-03-14T10:09:00Z — 2026-03-14T10:15:00Z (mitigated at 10:13:30Z when canary traffic removed)
- affected: ~12 orgs, ~0.2% of global requests at peak
- user-visible: UI stalls in streaming editors (workaround: refresh or re-initiate stream)

ashley (oncall): I'm adding customer-impact tags and notifying support for proactive outreach to top affected accounts.

ops-runner: orchestration rollback decided? we left v10 at 0% but config remains. If eng wants a full rollback (revoke v10 from catalog), ops can run revoke: `orchestrator revoke --model v10 --reason "regression: kv/cache/kernel"`

jonas: don't revoke yet — need artifacts for root cause. I'll collect logs and run a repro with a smaller load against v10 on staging with debug kernels enabled.

mia: putting a canary hold tag on v10 and disabling auto-rollout: `/components/canary/v10 hold` (internal command executed).

deploy-bot: NOTE: Canary v10 marked HOLD by mia. Auto-rollout disabled.

ashley (oncall): handoff: I'm going offline for a focused meeting, leaving oncall monitoring to alerts only. Jonas, I'll ping you in 30m for status. If latency regresses or error rate increases, page immediately.

jonas: acknowledged. I'll file post-incident and include timeline, mitigation commands executed, and a checklist for kernel+cache regression tests.

mia: quick follow-up: impl note — fallback policy should consider sustained tail latency (p99) as a trigger, not only error rate. Adding to ENG-PRI backlog.

ashley (oncall): thanks everyone. incident-bot: mark incident resolved for live mitigation — status: mitigated (traffic shift). Root-cause investigation in progress (assigned: eng-runtime / eng-ml).

incident-bot: Incident updated: mitigated=true, mitigation_action="canary traffic -> 0%", followup_ticket=ENG-INC-2026-312, severity=high.

jonas: starting deep-dive now, will update thread with logs and repro steps.

(reacted :thumbsup: by ashley (oncall))
